item.title: Respect your elders' riches: Why Older Americans Own the Economy
item.description:
People age 75+ are America's wealthiest...
Morning, sunshine. In today’s small business news, singer and talk show host Kelly Clarkson is beefing with a Brooklyn boutique she claims gave her the Pretty Woman treatment when she inquired about the price of a $15,000 bird automaton. After Clarkson put the store on social media blast, it responded that the item simply wasn’t for sale (though the singer claims there was a price tag). We’ve been on Team Clarkson since From Justin to Kelly , so in solidarity we plan to walk into a Rainforest Cafe and try to buy all the animatronic animals.

item.title: Horror Movie Brew: How Cheap Horror Conquered Hollywood
item.description:
The future of scary movies looks ominously bright...
Boo! We got you good, didn’t we? While you recover from that scare, prepare for several more: Today’s special edition is all about the business of horror movies. We’ll get into how they became such a reliable moneymaker, why Hollywood is mining the internet for new talent and story ideas, the debate surrounding “elevated” horror, and much more. Lock the doors and grab your blankie—it’s time to put on Horror Movie Brew.

item.title: The cost of cozy: AI Solves Math as Heating Bills Soar
item.description:
The price of heating oil is spiking this winter...
This is your captain speaking. PSA: Do not dial in to your Zoom on an airplane. With in-flight wi-fi becoming the norm, reports are growing of people taking meetings in the sky. But the etiquette here is much clearer than the polarizing question of whether it’s ok to recline your seat—no one wants to involuntarily come along to your all-hands unless it’s the meeting where the tension between Jane from HR and Brad from accounting finally boils over.
